faqs.question: What does the AFB-Smear Examination by Fluorescent Stain – Tissue/Biopsy measure?
faqs.answer: This test measures the presence of acid-fast bacilli (AFB) specific to Mycobacterium tuberculosis in tissue or biopsy samples.

faqs.question: Why is AFB-Smear Examination by Fluorescent Stain – Tissue/Biopsy done?
faqs.answer: • To diagnose infection caused by tuberculosis • To monitor the effectiveness of tuberculosis treatment • To detect drug resistance in tuberculosis • To rule out tuberculosis infection in individuals with symptoms or risk factors

faqs.question: When is AFB-Smear Examination by Fluorescent Stain – Tissue/Biopsy recommended and who should take the test?
faqs.answer: This test may be recommended if you • Have symptoms suggestive of tuberculosis, such as persistent cough, weight loss, and night sweats. • Have been exposed to someone with active tuberculosis. • Are at a higher risk of developing tuberculosis, such as individuals with weakened immune systems or certain medical conditions.

faqs.question: What if the results of the AFB-Smear Examination by Fluorescent Stain – Tissue/Biopsy are abnormal?
faqs.answer: Abnormal results, i.e., results indicating the presence of acid-fast bacilli in the tissue or biopsy sample may indicate an active tuberculosis infection.

faqs.question: What to expect during the AFB-Smear Examination by Fluorescent Stain – Tissue/Biopsy?
faqs.answer: • A tissue or biopsy sample will be taken from the affected area, such as lungs or lymph nodes. • The sample will be processed and stained with a fluorescent dye for examination under a fluorescent microscope.

faqs.question: What preparations are required before the AFB-Smear Examination by Fluorescent Stain – Tissue/Biopsy?
faqs.answer: • Inform your doctor about any ongoing medications or allergies. • The specific site and type of tissue sample required will be explained by your doctor. • Follow any fasting instructions provided by your doctor, if applicable. Please reach out to your healthcare provider for any specific requirements.

faqs.question: What other tests may be ordered with AFB-Smear Examination by Fluorescent Stain – Tissue/Biopsy?
faqs.answer: Other tests that may be ordered alongside AFB-Smear Examination by Fluorescent Stain – Tissue/Biopsy include: • Tuberculosis culture: This test helps identify the specific strain of tuberculosis bacteria and determine its drug susceptibility. • GeneXpert MTB/RIF: This molecular test detects the presence of tuberculosis bacteria and identifies drug resistance to rifampicin, a common tuberculosis medication.

faqs.question: What is the AFB-Smear Examination by Fluorescent Stain – Tissue/Biopsy also known as?
faqs.answer: Acid-Fast Bacilli Smear Examination by Fluorescence Microscopy

faqs.question: What is tuberculosis?
faqs.answer: Tuberculosis is a contagious infection caused by the bacteria Mycobacterium tuberculosis. It primarily affects the lungs but can also affect other parts of the body. Common symptoms include persistent cough, weight loss, fever, and night sweats. Early diagnosis and treatment are crucial for effective management.
